ledger.note: c. 370: the Alchons chase the Kidarites toward India. The Alchon page has them ruling Gandhara 'alongside' the Kidarites around 380-385; the Kidarites dossier keeps Bactria as Kidarite land, so both claims are drawn as contested until the Kidarites fall in 467.

c. 380-385: the Alchons emerge at Kapisa. 'c. 380-385: Alchons emerged in Kapisa, taking Kabulistan from the Sassanians'; the page notes they are 'sometimes said' to have taken Kabul in 388. The year is the start of the span.

region.text: the Hindu Kush country and its passes

ledger.note: c. 430: Khingila takes the Hindu Kush routes. 'c. 430: Khingila emerged and took control of Hindu Kush routes from the Kidarites.' The page names routes, not land: Bamyan is the reading (confidence 1).
c. 450: the Hephthalites take Bactria. 'Hephthalites took Bactria around 450 CE, and later Nezak-Alchons took over parts of the region.' The White Huns dossier starts its Kunduz core in 450.

460-470: the Alchons take Gandhara and the Punjab. '460-470: Alchons took Gandhara and the Punjab'; c. 460 they took Taxila and destroyed Buddhist monasteries there. The page names no previous holder; the Kidarite lands of the Gandhara side are the reading. [fx-23] Gandhara only. The Punjab half of this event moved to a separate gain of 470 from the gupta-empire dossier (see there): the Gupta Empire page has the Guptas keep their territory under Skandagupta (to 467) and lose 'control over much of western India after 467-469', while the Alchon page's window for the Punjab is 460-470.
467: the Kidarites fall. '467: Kidarites were defeated by Peroz I, with Alchon and Hephthalite aid under Mehama, ending Kidarite rule in Transoxiana.'

region.text: the Punjab (Pakistani and Indian Punjab, Haryana)

ledger.note: 470: the Alchons take the Punjab from the Guptas. Alchon page: 'Between 460 and 470 CE, the Alchons took over Gandhara and the Punjab' (window 460-470; the Gandhara half stays at 460). Gupta Empire page: the Skandagupta page has him 'maintain control of his inherited territory' (reign to 467) and the Gupta Empire page says 'the later Gupta coinage indicates their loss of control over much of western India after 467-469' and that 'much of the empire in the northwest was overrun by the Huns by 500'. The two windows meet at 467-470, so the Punjab is dated at the end of the Alchon page's span (the year is the researcher's reading; confidence 1). Before, this dossier drew the Punjab from 460 over Gupta land that the Gupta dossier still held (conflict, given to the Alchon by the size rule).

484: the Nezak branch takes Zabulistan. 'They took control of Zabulistan after the defeat and eventual death of Sassanian Emperor Peroz I' (infobox 'Established: 484'); the Nezak page says they 'may have been identical with Khingila of the Alchon Huns'.

region.text: Malwa, Gujarat, Rajasthan and the Gupta frontier

ledger.note: 515: the First Hunnic War ends (the page's span 496-515).
by 520: Mihirakula holds Sindh. 'Sindh: Conquered by 520 CE.' The page does not name the previous ruler.

520: the Second Hunnic War begins and Mihirakula occupies north India. '520: Second Hunnic War began, with Mihirakula at the Jhelum'; the war lasted 'after about 15 years of occupation' to c. 534; the Gwalior inscription 'Lord of the Earth' suggests his rule reached Gwalior.

c. 534: the Hunnic occupation ends. 'c. 534: The Second Hunnic War ended after about 15 years of occupation'; Yasodharman defeated Mihirakula at Sondani c. 528 (the Mihirakula page: 525-532, 'likely by 530'); Narasimhagupta Baladitya captured him.

by 542: the Punjab and Sindh are lost. 'Alchon possessions in the Punjab and north India were lost by 542'; the pages name no heir polity (the Yasodharman page is read by the white-huns dossier, not here), so the counterpart is nobody.

c. 560: the Sasanians and Western Turks may take Zabulistan. 'the Sasanians allied with the Western Turks against the Hephthalites, and they may have also wrestled control of Zabulistan from the Nezaks'. A maybe on the page: confidence 1.

625: the Western Turks take Gandhara. '625: The Western Turks took Khuttal and Kapisa-Gandhara, establishing the Yabghus of Tokharistan.' The Nezak page keeps the capital at Bagram (Kapisa) to 665, so only Gandhara is taken from this state; Kapisa is left to the Alchon in the Kabul valley (the pages disagree).
c. 630: the Kashmir line of the Alchons ends. 'c. 590-630: Narendraditya Khinkhila ruled'; the infobox lists the Karkota dynasty among the successors but no page opened dates the handover.

ledger.note: 670: the Alchon state ends. Infobox 'disestablished 670'; the Nezak page ends the principality in 665 (Turk Shahis 'probably first in Kabul and later throughout the territory'). The land passes to the Turk Shahis and, briefly, to Arab raids (the Nezak page: Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura occupied Kabul in 665; the last ruler was Ghar-ilchi).

wars.name: Alchon-Kidarite wars
wars.outcome: The Kidarites were chased toward India from c. 370 and defeated in 467 by Peroz I with Alchon and Hephthalite aid.
wars.note: The page also has Skandagupta defeating the Kidarites in c. 455.

wars.name: Skandagupta's Huna war
wars.outcome: Skandagupta defeated an unnamed Huna ruler c. 455-457 (Bhitari pillar); no land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: First Hunnic War

union.text: Kausambi, where one of Toramana's seals was found

wars.outcome: Toramana reached the Alchon maximum, took Malwa and Gujarat, was beaten at Eran in 510 by Bhanugupta (Toramana page) and defeated by Prakashadharma in 515.
wars.note: The Alchon page says Toramana probably prevailed at Eran.

wars.name: Second Hunnic War
wars.outcome: About fifteen years of occupation; Yasodharman beat Mihirakula at Sondani (c. 528); Narasimhagupta Baladitya captured him; ended c. 534; the Punjab was lost by 542.

wars.name: Hephthalite-Sasanian-Turk war
wars.outcome: The Hephthalites were defeated by the Sasanians and Western Turks (page: 557-565); the Sasanians may have taken Zabulistan.

wars.name: Arab invasions of Kabul
wars.outcome: An Arab army of about 6,000 in 654; Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura took Kabul after a siege in 665; a renewed offensive in 668. The Turk Shahis replaced the Nezaks.

certainty.note: A nomadic empire known from coins, seals and a few inscriptions (Eran, Risthal, Sanjeli); no page gives a border.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Alchon Huns). The white-huns dossier (ia-01-c) draws the Indian lands (Punjab, Sindh, Kashmir, Gujarat) in Cliopatria's White Huns shapes of 490-533 and records them as gains from 'alchon-huns'; the Alchon page now regards the Alchon as 'a separate entity', so a gap-filler should remove those Indian lands from white-huns and take them from here (this dossier draws them 460-541). The same overlap holds for the Kidarites (Bactria and Gandhara in 370-467, drawn as a contested zone) and for the Nezak Huns, whom the Nezak page makes a separate principality (484-665) at Kabul and Zabulistan: this dossier folds the Nezak lands in (the page says the Nezak 'may have been identical with Khingila'), and the Nezak Huns have no dossier of their own. The page gives no area. Rulers are not given: the page lists Khingila (430-495), Mehama (461-493), Toramana (493-515), Mihirakula (515-542 or 515-540) and a Kashmir line (Pravarasena c. 530-590, Gokarna c. 570-590, Narendraditya Khinkhila c. 590-630) with overlapping dates and no single succession. Udabhanda has no date on any page opened. Mehama 'governed for Peroz I' (461-493) and Toramana became a vassal 'likely under Yasodharman' after 515: neither is drawn as a vassal tint. The Eran result is disputed between the two pages (Toramana: beaten by Bhanugupta in 510; Alchon page: Toramana probably prevailed); no Eran event is in the ledger. Uttar Pradesh is named in Toramana's territory but only the Kausambi march is drawn. Aulikara dynasty of Malwa (Prakashadharma, Yasodharman) needs a dossier (not a Cliopatria row). Gazetteer names used: all in the gazetteer except Kausambi (a coordinate radius is used). [Reviewer ia-01-x, 2026-10-19] Cliopatria's Turk Shahis row (shapes from 561, 644 and 666) covers this dossier's Kabulistan, Bamyan and Zabulistan: 42 percent of keyframe alchon-huns_560 lies inside the Turk Shahi shape of 600 and all of alchon-huns_630 inside that of 650. The two double-draw 561-670 until the turk-shahis dossier (not yet written) starts its Kabul land around 665, as the Nezak page has it. [fx-23, 2026-11-01] The Punjab is drawn from 470, not 460 (ledger gain of 470 from gupta-empire, new keyframe alchon-huns_470): the Gupta dossier still held it until 469. The Indian lands and the Kabul fringe that white-huns drew in Cliopatria's White Huns shapes are now subtracted there (white-huns keyframes from 451), so this dossier alone draws them.
